title: Copilot Code Review and PR Workflow

questions.question: Which set of properties makes a pull request reviewable in this lesson's policy?
options: A short title, green CI, and a large diff with a clear headline
A linked issue and tests, even when the PR mixes unrelated changes
One bounded concern, stated intent, shipped verification, and a linked issue
A Copilot-generated summary that lets reviewers infer the reason for the change
questions.explanation: reviewability requires a bounded mental model first, then what-and-why intent, verification, and traceability to an issue. A fluent summary cannot replace those conditions.

questions.question: A PR has logical_changes=3 but only 12 files, intent, tests, and an issue link. What does reviewability return?
options: REVIEWABLE, because the file count is below 20
NEEDS CONTEXT, because the body needs more detail
REVIEWABLE, because tests and an issue link are present
NEEDS SPLIT, because the diff contains unrelated concerns
questions.explanation: The policy checks logical_changes first. More than one unrelated concern requires a split before the remaining review criteria can make the PR reviewable.

questions.question: A PR has 21 changed files, one logical concern, intent, tests, and an issue link. Which verdict follows?
options: NEEDS SPLIT
REVIEWABLE
NEEDS CONTEXT
FALSE POSITIVE
questions.explanation: Even one coherent concern is too large for this policy when files_changed exceeds 20. reviewability returns NEEDS_SPLIT before checking the later fields.

questions.question: A bounded PR states its intent and links an issue but ships no test or other verification. What does reviewability return?
options: REVIEWABLE
NEEDS CONTEXT
NEEDS SPLIT
FIX
questions.explanation: After the size and intent checks, the missing verification triggers NEEDS_CONTEXT. A plausible PR description does not demonstrate that the change works.

questions.question: triage receives a low-confidence nit that matches an allowed repository policy. Which disposition wins?
options: FIX, because every bot comment should change code
WONTFIX, because the confidence is below 0.8
FALSE_POSITIVE, because the repository explicitly permits the pattern
NEEDS CONTEXT, because nits cannot be classified
questions.explanation: matches_repo_policy is checked first and returns FALSE_POSITIVE regardless of category or confidence. The policy, not an unnecessary code change, is the correct place to resolve the mismatch.

questions.question: How does triage classify a bug comment with confidence=0.9 that does not match repository policy?
options: WONTFIX, because automated comments are advisory
FALSE_POSITIVE, because confidence is not certainty
NEEDS CONTEXT, because only security comments are actionable
FIX, because a bug at or above 0.6 clears the action threshold
questions.explanation: With no policy exception, bug and security comments at confidence 0.6 or higher are actionable. triage therefore returns FIX for this 0.9 bug report.
